claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 was originally produced in a hierarchical heterostructured state with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Fluctuation amplitude, spatial correlation length, and phase-distribution metrics can quantitatively capture the mechanically relevant hierarchy of HfNbTiVAl10.
Imaging-derived phase-distribution descriptors can help predict mechanical behavior.
The reduced microstructural descriptors mediate dislocation propagation behavior.
The reduced microstructural descriptors mediate crack propagation behavior.
A model combining reduced thermophysical inputs with imaging-derived descriptors can learn the nonlinear mapping from structure to Young's modulus.
A model combining reduced thermophysical inputs with imaging-derived descriptors can learn the nonlinear mapping from structure to yield strength.
A model combining reduced thermophysical inputs with imaging-derived descriptors can learn the nonlinear mapping from structure to fracture toughness.
The proposed reduced model can replace full-scale CALPHAD and first-principles simulations for these predictions.
A limited set of high-throughput experiments is sufficient to calibrate the proposed model.
The proposed model will reduce prediction time by approximately 50% relative to full-scale simulation methods.
Predictions of Young's modulus will be within 10–15% of experimental measurements.
Predictions of yield strength will be within 10–15% of experimental measurements.
Predictions of fracture toughness will be within 10–15% of experimental measurements.
Detailed CALPHAD, first-principles, and high-dimensional machine-learning approaches require enormous computational resources and have low efficiency.
Existing approaches have lower predictive accuracy for fracture toughness than the proposed model.
The model will become unreliable when omitted extreme inhomogeneities, unforeseen phase interactions, or sub-micrometer fluctuations materially affect dislocation mobility or crack propagation.
Processing-induced defects such as surface cracks will make the model unreliable when their effects are not represented by the descriptors.
Deviation exceeding 15% for any target property or time savings below 50% is specified as a falsifying result.
